items.title: Kelantan couple struggle to afford sick son's special milk, resort to rice water
items.summary: Siti Noor Mastubaidura Ariffin, 36, said she had been running a small grocery business but was forced to close it to care for her 12-year-old son, Muhammad Aiman Mohamed, who requires constant attention. "I prioritise spending his earnings on Muhammad Aiman's needs, including milk, disposable diapers and other care supplies. Siti Noor Mastubaidura said Muhammad Aiman suffered four seizures within two months when he was eight, resulting in brain damage due to an infection.

items.title: Budget 2027: Tax breaks to encourage corporate support for food bank initiative, says Armizan
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — A special tax deduction incentive for the Ihsan Food Bank Initiative (i-FB) under Budget 2027 is expected to encourage greater participation by strategic partners, including the corporate sector, in strengthening the food bank ecosystem. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the government had agreed to grant special tax deductions to parties contributing food and equipment for the i-FB initiative from January 1 next year until December 31, 2030. Armizan said the detailed mechanism for implementing the special tax deduction incentive for i-FB would be coordinated with the Finance Ministry.

items.title: Two men held after car crashes into drain while fleeing police
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Two men suspected of stealing cables were arrested after the car they were travelling in crashed into a drain while fleeing from police in Taman Sri Watan, Ampang, yesterday. Ampang Jaya police chief ACP Khairul Anuar Khalid said police received a tip-off from the public at about 5.53am. He said a police patrol spotted a blue Perodua Aruz without registration plates parked along Jalan Watan 8.

items.title: CM: Penang ready to work with Putrajaya on new elderly care, research centre
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 11 — Penang is ready to work with the federal government to establish the National Integrated Care Centres of Excellence (NICE) in the state as part of efforts to prepare for an ageing population. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the state government would cooperate in implementing the initiative, announced in Budget 2027 yesterday, which aims to provide training, research and care facilities for the elderly. “We certainly welcome it and the state government will provide cooperation to ensure this facility can be established in Penang,” he told reporters after officiating the second State Heritage Declaration Ceremony under the Penang State Heritage Enactment 2011 for 2026 here yesterday.

items.title: Trump says Putin 'would like to see a settlement' in Ukraine war
items.summary: JOINT BASE ANDREWS: US President Donald Trump said on Saturday that his Russian counterpart Vladimir Putin would like to reach a deal on the war in Ukraine, accusing Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of resisting a compromise. "Russia would like to make a deal... but for whatever reason, Zelenskyy does not want to make a deal," Trump told reporters. Zelenskyy called Trump's diesel deal with Moscow a "weak decision".

items.title: South Korea completes Arctic-Europe commercial voyage, eyes regular service despite risks
items.summary: SEOUL, (South Korea): A South Korean container ship completed the country's first commercial round trip to Europe via the Arctic on Sunday, as authorities bank on the route helping turn the port of Busan into a global maritime hub. Authorities say the Arctic route could cut typical voyage times by around a third. President Lee Jae Myung has made Arctic shipping a priority, and officials hope to launch regular services by 2030.

items.title: Budget 2027: RM1.1b for enforcement agencies signals stronger anti-corruption push, says MACC
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The RM1.1 billion allocation to enhance the operational capabilities of law enforcement agencies, including the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), reflects the government’s strong commitment to combating crime, including corruption, and strengthening national governance. According to the MACC, the government’s emphasis on drafting the Government-Owned Entities Bill to tighten the governance of entities entrusted with managing public funds and assets reflects a commitment that goes beyond merely combating abuse of power to actively strengthening governance. “The government’s decision to disclose project information, including contractors and contract values following the Government Procurement Act which will take effect next year, also reflects the government’s transparency in sharing information with the public,” according to the statement.

items.title: Budget 2027: Health Ministry to expand outsourcing programme to cut waiting times
items.summary: Deputy Health Director-General (Medical) Datuk Dr Mohd Azman Yacob said the additional allocation would enable the ministry to refer more patients to private hospitals for faster treatment. Introduced in 2024, HSOP currently benefits patients requiring treatment in nephrology, cardiology, cardiothoracic surgery, paediatric cardiology and radiology. Mohd Azman said HSOP enabled patients to access treatment at private hospitals more quickly, while the charges imposed remained subject to the rates set by government hospitals.

items.title: Budget 2027: New immigration quarters planned for Perak, Sabah
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — The construction of new quarters at the Langkap Immigration Detention Depot in Perak and Papar, Sabah, under Budget 2027 will improve the welfare and operational readiness of Immigration Department (JIM) personnel in carrying out enforcement duties. Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said more conducive residential facilities would not only enhance the well-being of officers and their families, but also help them focus fully on their responsibilities in law enforcement and immigration detainee management. He said personnel welfare was not merely about providing facilities, but also formed the foundation of an enforcement organisation’s readiness and effectiveness.

items.title: Jais probes allegations of a Muslim taking part in another religion's rituals
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (JAIS) is investigating a viral social media post about an individual believed to be Muslim who allegedly took part in religious rituals of another faith that contravene Islamic law. Director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said JAIS had launched the investigation under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, which cover acts of worship carried out in violation of Islamic law and acts that bring Islam into disrepute. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said his department noted that the videos were also linked to alleged acts of worship and the use of certain incantations.

items.title: MCMC probes Facebook post suspected of insulting Islam by mocking Quranic verse
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has launched an investigation into an individual over Facebook content suspected of insulting Islam. MCMC said the content concerned the use of the word “lighad”, which refers to verse 18 of Surah al-Hashr, in Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s Budget 2027 speech on Friday. “The content allegedly mocked a Quranic verse, causing concern among the public,” it said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia seen trading within 1,600-1,630 points range next week with cautious upside bias
items.summary: Operating expenditure accounts for RM376.8 billion, while RM83 billion has been allocated for development expenditure (DE). Education receives the largest allocation at almost RM69 billion, followed by health at RM47.7 billion and security with RM44 billion allocation. Weekly turnover advanced to 19.63 billion units worth RM15.72 billion from 17.39 billion units worth RM14.42 billion in the previous week.

items.title: Cops arrest five men after video of alleged armed assault in Petaling Jaya goes viral
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Police have arrested five men, aged between 30 and 40, on suspicion of being involved in an attack on a man using dangerous weapons at a housing area in Petaling Jaya on Friday. Petaling Jaya District Police Chief ACP Shamsudin Mamat said that during the arrests, police also seized a machete and a saw believed to have been used in the incident. “At 1.03am yesterday (Friday), the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters (IPD) received a police report from a local man stating that he had been attacked by several individuals.

items.title: Ringgit expected to strengthen next week amid more cues from 2027 Budget
items.summary: Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said market attention would remain on 2027 Budget, with economists and analysts expected to examine the details and implications in the coming days. "There are some measures, such as a tax cut for the M40 income group and more measures on the guarantees for SMEs via institutions such as Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) and Credit Guarantee Corporation (CGC). Anwar also announced that Syarikat Jaminan Pembiayaan Perniagaan Bhd (SJPP) and Credit Guarantee Corporation Malaysia Bhd (CGC) would provide up to RM32 billion in financing guarantees next year.

items.title: Jais probes viral post alleging Muslim took part in non-Islamic religious ritual
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 11 — The Selangor Islamic Religious Department (Jais) is investigating a viral post concerning an individual believed to be Muslim who allegedly performed rituals of another religion in violation of Islamic law. Jais director Datuk Mohd Shahzihan Ahmad said investigations had begun under Sections 4 and 10 of the Syariah Criminal Offences (Selangor) Enactment 1995, which cover acts of demonstrating worship in ways that contravene Islamic law and bringing Islam into contempt, according to a report by Bernama. Yesterday, the media reported that the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) was taking action with the relevant authorities over the circulation of several video recordings allegedly showing a Muslim individual participating in non-Islamic religious rituals.

items.title: FRIM, IIUM Braille book opens doors for visually impaired to explore endangered forest trees
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The visually impaired can now learn about endangered forest tree species in Malaysia through a tactile and Braille book produced by the Forest Research Institute Malaysia (FRIM) and the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM). FRIM director-general Datuk Dr Ismail Parlan said the initiative reflected efforts to make the country's forest heritage accessible to everyone, including the visually impaired. Ismail said FRIM was ready to collaborate with various parties on similar initiatives to benefit the visually impaired.

items.title: Malaysia, Indonesia discuss joint action to tackle transboundary haze
items.summary: JAKARTA, Oct 11 — Indonesia has confirmed that discussions with Malaysia are underway to detail the best form of cooperation to tackle forest and land fires that have triggered transboundary haze. Indonesian Communications Agency head Syahganda Nainggolan said good relations between the two countries were an important foundation for finding joint solutions, particularly as firefighting operations faced challenges, including natural factors. “Malaysia’s Foreign Minister and Indonesia’s Foreign Minister are holding detailed discussions to find solutions and jointly address the forest and land fires,” he told the media on Saturday.

items.title: Tax deductions for Food Bank donors to begin in 2027
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Special tax deductions for food and equipment donors under the Ihsan Food Bank Initiative (i-FB) will take effect from Jan 1, 2027, to Dec 31, 2030. Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the incentive was aimed at encouraging wider participation from the corporate sector, voluntary organisations and other strategic partners in helping those in need. Armizan said the incentive would also recognise and encourage contributions of food, equipment and operational support to strengthen the implementation of i-FB.

items.title: Two women die after car skids into opposite lane, collides with trailer in Terengganu five-vehicle crash
items.summary: Setiu District Police chief Supt Zahril Asri Mohd Zain said police received information about the crash at about 4pm, while the incident is believed to have occurred at 3.45pm. He said initial investigations showed that the Proton Waja travelling from Kota Bharu towards Kuala Terengganu was believed to have skidded into the opposite lane before colliding with a Mercedes-Benz trailer. “Following the collision, the trailer also skidded and grazed a Perodua Aruz multi-purpose vehicle (MPV), a Perodua Myvi and a UDT lorry travelling from Kota Bharu towards Kuala Terengganu,” he said in a statement yesterday.

items.title: #NSTViral: Ministry officer rejects 'settlement' offer during cooking oil raid
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry enforcement officer has drawn praise online after rejecting an apparent attempt to negotiate an informal settlement during a raid on suspected hoarders of subsidised cooking oil. If you want to talk somewhere else, I'll take you straight to MACC (Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission), nowhere else, just MACC," the officer warned. "Top-class officer.

items.title: MACC sets up special team to re-examine RM350,000 corruption allegations against its senior officer
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has established a special team to review and re-examine corruption allegations amounting to RM350,000 involving one of its senior officers. MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the directive to form the special team was issued immediately following recent calls and the resurfacing of the issue online. Malaysian Corruption Watch (MCW) had earlier urged the MACC and the Anti-Corruption Advisory Board (ACAB) to take immediate action regarding allegations of accepting a bribe of approximately RM350,000 linked to a senior MACC officer.

items.title: Execution survivor released from hospital, returns to prison
items.summary: TENNESSEE, (United States): Death row inmate Christa Pike was released from a US hospital on Saturday and sent back to prison where she will continue receiving medical care following her botched execution attempt in Tennessee, her attorneys said. Pike was discharged from a local hospital and is now at the Debra K. Johnson Rehabilitation Center, where she has been housed for more than 30 years, said attorneys Stephen Ferrell and Luke Ihnen from Federal Defender Services of Eastern Tennessee, and Randy Spivey and Kelly Gleason from the Tennessee Office of the Post Conviction Defender in a joint release. Pike, sentenced to death for a 1995 murder, awoke "angry and confused" in the hospital this week with a long recuperation ahead after surviving the attempted execution on September 30, her lawyers said on Wednesday.

items.title: Haze: Schools in Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu to operate as usual today, says Fadhlina
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual today as the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings in the three states remain under control. “Schools in Kedah, Kelantan and Terengganu will operate as usual tomorrow (October 11) as the API readings are still under control,” she said in a statement yesterday. In a statement yesterday, MOE said the committee, comprising State Education Departments (JPN) and District Education Offices (PPD), will monitor API readings at scheduled times daily.

items.title: Johor extends school closures until Oct 16 as haze worsens
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 11 — The Johor government has decided to extend the closure of all schools and educational institutions in the state for five days, from October 12 to 16, due to the haze. State Education and Information Committee chairman Dr Muhammad Naqib Md Ghazali said the decision was made upon the decree of the Regent of Johor, Tunku Mahkota Ismail, following the worsening air quality. Muhammad Naqib said the decision also took into account several key factors based on an assessment of the current situation, including projected wind movements from Kalimantan, Indonesia, between October 13 and 15, which could bring transboundary air pollution and affect air quality in the state.

items.title: Haze eases as Langkawi, Balik Pulau record healthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Haze conditions showed significant improvement today, with Langkawi and Balik Pulau recording healthy air pollutant index (API) readings. Langkawi, Kedah, recorded an API reading of 36, while Balik Pulau, Penang, registered 28. This was an improvement from yesterday, when no locations nationwide recorded healthy API readings.

items.title: Man dies after entering tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park
items.summary: LONDON: A man has died in a tiger attack after entering the animal's enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park, police said, PA Media and dpa reported. His family have since been informed, South Yorkshire Police (SYP) said. A police spokesperson said: "At 1.35pm today, we received reports of a man entering a tiger enclosure at Yorkshire Wildlife Park.

items.title: Tanker catches fire after being struck by unknown projectile in Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: ISTANBUL: A tanker caught fire after being struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz, the UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Sunday, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The master of the outbound tanker reported that the vessel was struck on its port side by an unknown projectile, causing a fire on board, UKMTO said. It said the tanker struck a mine while trying to exit via the alternative route, triggering an explosion visible from coastal areas.

items.title: Saudi-led coalition vows 'firm' response after 12 killed in attack on Riyadh airport
items.summary: ISTANBUL: The Saudi-led coalition in Yemen vowed early Sunday to respond "firmly" to an attack on the main airport in the capital Riyadh, which authorities said killed 12 people and injured 309 others, Anadolu Ajansi reported. Al-Maliki said the attack constituted a war crime under international humanitarian law and customary rules. He said the coalition's Joint Forces Command would respond "firmly" and in line with international humanitarian law.

items.title: IKEA Malaysia focusing on affordability and quality
items.summary: BATU KAWAN: IKEA Malaysia is prioritising affordable, quality home furnishing and storage solutions under its financial year 2027 strategy, helping Malaysians maximise existing spaces without costly renovations. Its country retail director Takeshi Murai said the focus on storage and organisation stemmed from extensive customer research and home visits, which revealed a strong desire among Malaysians to organise their belongings more effectively. We want to be low price, which means we design our products and solutions with quality," Murai said.

items.title: Learn from India before Malayan tiger falls silent
items.summary: Malaysia should pay close attention. Our Malayan tiger is not merely another endangered species. We have the National Tiger Conservation Action Plan.

items.title: 'Throw the book' at lorry firms over road accidents, experts say [WATCH]
items.summary: fuadnizam@nst.com.my KUALA LUMPUR: Authorities should throw the book at lorry companies for road accidents involving their drivers, a road safety activist and a criminologist said. The employers must face legal consequences for negligence and failure to enforce safety measures, they added. Road safety activist Tan Sri Lee Lam Thye said such incidents have occurred repeatedly despite warnings from authorities, including the transport minister, with dangerous driving, driving under the influence and vehicle overloading continuing to endanger lives.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Elderly care plans face execution test
items.summary: Therefore, the 2027 Budget has raised hopes of greater support, but elderly care service providers and senior citizens say effective implementation will be key to easing the strain. Fong said the allocation of more than RM40 million to train 8,000 people for the elderly care sector could help address the shortage of caregivers. Senior care activist Tony Lian, who runs several charitable care centres, said elderly care should be a shared responsibility rather than a burden borne by individuals and their families.

items.title: Haze: Malaysian, Singaporean firms under investigation
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: JOHOR BARU: A Malaysian plantation group and several Singapore-linked companies have been linked to Indonesian concessions where fire hotspots were detected. A report by Greenpeace Indonesia, Greenpeace Malaysia and Pantau Gambut identified at least one Malaysian company alongside four concessions linked to Singapore-based companies. Indonesian Consul-General in Johor Baru Sigit Suryantoro Widiyanto said they identified 57 businesses across eight provinces in their enforcement crackdown.

items.title: 2027 Budget: Budi Belia 'a good starting point'
items.summary: The proposed Budi Belia e-wallet incentive under the 2027 Budget could draw more youths into community work, particularly students who struggle to meet expenses, but those already volunteering say sustaining their interest will take more than financial rewards. Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM) veterinary student Yaashinii Naaidu Sri Sivabalasundram, 22, who volunteers at the Furry Kids Safe Haven dog shelter in Rantau, Negri Sembilan, said the money could help cover transport, meals and other expenses. But Yaashinii said she would continue volunteering even without the incentive because of her commitment to animal welfare.

items.title: Traumatised Panamanians begin quake recovery
items.summary: CHITRE: Residents near the epicentre of a major earthquake in southern Panama began cleaning up on Saturday, traumatised by the previous day's heavy shaking that left widespread damage but, so far, no reported deaths. We weren't prepared for this kind of event," said Aldulfo Quintero as he cleared debris from a store in Chitre, about 250km southwest of Panama City. Like many others in Chitre, the capital of hard-hit Herrera province, 28-year-old Yakshuri Castillo chose to sleep outdoors due to fears of another quake.

items.title: RM10,000 duty-free shopping coming to Langkawi and Labuan: What can you buy?
items.summary: While both islands offer a wide range of duty-free goods, shoppers hoping to make the most of the higher allowance may want to focus on items that usually cost more on the mainland. The availability of specific brands may also vary between retailers and the two islands. Under existing rules, different limits apply to goods such as clothing, cosmetics, food products and alcoholic beverages.

items.title: Malaysia has spent decades digitising public healthcare. Why are paper records still in use?
items.summary: Registration is recorded electronically, appointments are managed through the hospital’s information system, and doctors can retrieve a patient’s medical information without having to wait for a physical folder to arrive from another department. The idea behind an electronic medical record (EMR) is straightforward: instead of a patient’s medical history being stored primarily in paper files, the information is recorded and managed digitally, allowing authorised healthcare personnel to retrieve it when needed. But Malaysia is still in the process of making that transition across its public healthcare system.

items.title: Palestinian Mahmoud Abu Hamda wins top photography prize at Bayeux
items.summary: BAYEUX: Palestinian freelancer Mahmoud Abu Hamda on Saturday won the photography category at the prestigious Bayeux award for war correspondents for his work from Gaza. The Washington Post, NPR (National Public Radio, US) and CNN won the top prizes in the print, radio and television categories for reports from Ukraine, Gaza and the West Bank respectively. As well as the top prize, Hamda, who is based in the Gaza Strip, also won the Public's Choice award for his reportage "What War Leaves Behind".

items.title: Power restored in eastern Cuba after outage
items.summary: HAVANA: Power was restored in eastern Cuba on Saturday, several hours after an outage caused by a partial grid failure, the national power company said, as the island reels from a months-long US oil blockade. "The partial disconnection of the national grid in the eastern region is over," Union Electrica de Cuba (UNE) said. Cuba, a nation of 9.4 million people, has suffered repeated power outages, and rolling blackouts can last up to 20 hours a day.

items.title: Macron popularity lowest since taking office
items.summary: PARIS: French President Emmanuel Macron's popularity has fallen to its lowest level since taking office in 2017, according to a poll published on Saturday. The poll comes as France faces record fuel prices and protests by high school students, with respondents citing purchasing power as their top concern. Among politicians seen as potential successors to Macron, far-right leaders Jordan Bardella and Marine Le Pen remained the most popular, with approval ratings of 33 and 32 per cent respectively.

items.title: Brazil's Lula accuses Meta of election interference
items.summary: BRASILIA: The campaign of Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva accused tech giant Meta of election interference on Saturday after his social media content was allegedly blocked on the company's platforms. In a statement, Lula's campaign reported instances where platforms owned by Meta — the parent company of Facebook, WhatsApp and Instagram — allegedly restricted the distribution of his content. It also said that prior to last Sunday's first round of voting — in which Flavio Bolsonaro finished first — the profiles of Lula and other leftist leaders "suddenly disappeared from Instagram's search function".

items.title: [UPDATED] Attack on Saudi airport leaves 12 dead, dozens wounded
items.summary: RIYADH: The third attack this week on Riyadh's international airport on Saturday left at least 12 people dead and more than 300 wounded, Saudi authorities said, and the Iran-backed Houthis claimed responsibility for the strike, a major escalation of their campaign against the Saudis. The dead included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority said. Hospitals were flooded with wounded people brought by ambulance and helicopter, people briefed on the matter said.

items.title: Nine people, including children, dead after mass shooting in Pennsylvania
items.summary: The shooter, who has yet to be identified, died of an apparent self-inflicted wound before officers arrived at the scene, said Erie Police Chief Rick Lorah. This is one of those tragic scenes," Lorah said. Police have yet to establish a motive, Lorah said.

items.title: Evacuations, injuries at Riyadh airport after alleged Houthi attack
items.summary: RIYADH, Saudi Arabia: Yemen's Houthis attacked Riyadh's international airport with a missile on Saturday, a diplomatic source told AFP, with dozens reported wounded and a witness describing panic in the terminal. "Houthis are attacking civilian targets. Riyadh airport is a civilian target," the diplomatic source told AFP, saying the airport was hit by "a missile around 3pm" (1200 GMT).

items.title: Today's news in pictures - Saturday, Oct 10, 2026

items.title: Unauthorised oil blending could tarnish Malaysia’s global image, experts warn
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Oil blending activities must obtain written approval from the Customs director-general where required under the relevant regulations, and be backed by complete documentation to ensure legal compliance and transparent transactions, an expert said. Maritime, Customs and cross-border trade policy and law expert Madzli Harun said every activity involving the import, storage, blending and re-export of oil must be carried out within the scope of the licence and the conditions set by the authorities. Madzli said incomplete documentation, or discrepancies between records and the actual condition of the cargo, could raise questions over the declaration of goods, regulatory compliance and tax treatment.

items.title: Better roads, stronger pitch: MB sees Budget 2027 lifting Negeri Sembilan’s investment appeal
items.summary: Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said the construction of a new road from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Bandar Enstek was among the key infrastructure facilities that would support development in the area, while facilitating movement and improving accessibility. “Alhamdulillah, Negeri Sembilan is not being left behind in benefiting from Budget 2027 announced yesterday. The new road will also complement the development of MVV 2.0.

items.title: Anwar: Budget 2027 will balance fiscal discipline with cost-of-living relief
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — The government will continue to focus on prudent fiscal management in Budget 2027 to return benefits to the people and reduce cost-of-living pressures, especially for low-income households, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, also the finance minister, said although Malaysia’s inflation rate is around two per cent, one of the lowest in the world, the public still feels cost-of-living pressures due to rising prices of goods and certain services. Anwar said the government’s fiscal space has improved through more disciplined financial management, but these savings must be safeguarded from erosion by leakages and waste.

items.title: Anwar says reduced waste and leakages created room for more Budget 2027 aid
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Budget 2027 is the result of good national financial management, with the savings achieved now being returned to the people rather than enjoyed only by certain groups, says Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government had to resolve the country’s financial priorities first before gaining a greater capacity to channel savings to the people. Anwar said good governance practices allowed the government to provide various forms of assistance and initiatives to the people, including the provision of sports shoes and aid for rubber smallholders and padi farmers.

items.title: Budget 2027 more than numbers, says Anwar — it is a promise to the people
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today stressed that Budget 2027 is a covenant between the country and its leadership and the people, which must be implemented with full trust and integrity. The finance minister said the Fifth Madani Budget, formulated by a large team under the Ministry of Finance and other ministries, took into account the needs of various segments of society, ranging from driving economic growth to addressing issues concerning employment, wages and minimum income “We want to remind all Malaysians from various walks of life that this budget is not merely about managing finances, but must be an agreement bound by a covenant. “This means a promise, pledge or oath between the country, its leadership and the people.

items.title: Melaka tourist spots remain busy despite unhealthy API readings
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 10 — Tourist spots around Banda Hilir here continue to draw local and foreign visitors despite Melaka recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings since Thursday due to the haze. A Bernama check at the Stadthuys and Jonker Walk found that tourists were still visiting the popular attractions, while souvenir and handicraft shops remained open as usual. Asmah Zulkifli, 66, from Kuala Lumpur, said the haze had not deterred her and several friends from visiting tourist attractions, including the Stadthuys, after attending a friend’s wedding reception in Bukit Katil here.

items.title: Grieving mother haunted by memories of her three children killed in Pontian accident
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The mother of the three siblings who tragically died in an accident at Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong here, admits that she still finds it difficult to look at her children’s clothes and school bags as they serve as painful reminders of them. Julaiha Munaji, 44, said the simultaneous loss of Nor Daniel Aiman Norlizan, 18, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha Norlizan, 8, is the heaviest trial she and her family have ever faced. “I have six children, five boys and one girl.

items.title: DPM Zahid wants tahfiz graduates equipped for careers in technology, engineering and medicine
items.summary: BANGI, Oct 10 — Tahfiz graduates should have wider opportunities to pursue higher education and professional careers in fields such as technology, engineering and medicine to meet the country’s evolving workforce needs, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said. He said tahfiz education should go beyond Quran memorisation by equipping graduates with the knowledge, skills and qualifications needed to pursue a broader range of careers. Ahmad Zahid, who is also Rural and Regional Development Minister, said efforts to strengthen tahfiz education included enhancing the National Tahfiz Education Policy, developing the Malaysian Tahfiz Recognition Standard and strengthening pathways through the Malaysian Tahfiz Certificate to broaden graduates’ education and career options.

items.title: Air quality acceptable for now, Kedah schools to open as usual tomorrow
items.summary: The Kedah State Education Department (JPN) said in a statement that this was, however, subject to any further directives from the Ministry of Education and the relevant authorities. “The API readings are below 100, so all educational institutions in Kedah will operate as usual,” the statement said. The Kedah JPN said school administrators and educational institutions had nevertheless been reminded to remain alert to the latest developments, monitor API readings through official Department of Environment channels and take appropriate measures to ensure the safety and health of students and education personnel.

items.title: Lights on: Works Department to extend streetlight operating hours during haze
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 10 — The Public Works Department (JKR) will extend the operating hours of its streetlights by up to two hours during haze conditions to help improve visibility for road users. Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Ahmad Maslan said the measure, implemented through JKR’s Electrical Engineering Branch, was prompted by haze conditions that had reduced visibility and increased the risk of accidents. During haze conditions, the operating hours can be extended by up to two hours.

items.title: Fahmi urges Malaysians to prioritise mental health in World Mental Health Day post
items.summary: He said mental health should be cared for alongside physical health, particularly when dealing with the demands of work, family and everyday life. “In the midst of busy work, family and daily life, do not forget to look after our mental health just as we look after our physical health,” he said in a Facebook post in conjunction with World Mental Health Day today. World Mental Health Day is observed on October 10 every year to raise public awareness of the importance of mental health worldwide.

items.title: President El-Sisi invites Malaysia’s King, PM to visit Egypt
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 10 — Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi has extended an invitation to His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to visit Egypt. The president, who is on a two-day state visit to Malaysia, also thanked Sultan Ibrahim for conferring the Darjah Utama Seri Mahkota Negara (DMN) on him at Istana Negara earlier today. “It speaks much to the depth and strength of the relations between our two countries,” he said at a joint press conference with Anwar at the Seri Perdana Complex, Putrajaya today.

items.title: Egypt president El-Sisi praises Malaysia for helping injured Gazans, backs Palestinian state
items.summary: He said the Palestinian issue remained central to West Asia and was among the key matters discussed during his meeting with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. El-Sisi also commended Malaysia’s support for the Palestinian people, particularly its humanitarian assistance and efforts to provide medical treatment for injured Palestinians from Gaza. “I would be remiss if I didn't applaud Malaysia's supporting stance regarding the Palestinian issue and its keenness to provide humanitarian assistance to the Palestinian people and also hosting Palestinian second-injured people to get medical care here in Malaysia,” he said.

items.title: Malaysia and Egypt eye easier travel, more business as trade surges, says PM
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 10 — Malaysia and Egypt will focus on expanding trade and investment cooperation, improving flight connectivity and exploring new areas of economic collaboration at a Joint Commission meeting in the first quarter of next year. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the meeting, agreed upon by the two countries’ foreign ministers, would provide a platform to translate growing bilateral ties into broader economic opportunities. He said Malaysia saw considerable potential to expand cooperation with Egypt in several sectors, including semiconductors, electrical and electronics (E&E), agriculture and pharmaceuticals.

items.title: Health Ministry drafting national registry for persons with disabilities to improve service planning
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 10 — The Ministry of Health (MOH), through its Family Health Development Division’s Persons with Disabilities (PWD) Sector, has initiated strategic discussions on the development of the MOH PWD Strategic Plan. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the ministry was also drafting a proposal for a national-level PWD Registry (OKU Registry), which would incorporate data and needs profiles of the cerebral palsy (CP) community. Speaking to reporters, Dzulkefly said the strategic plan was still at an early stage, but it was important to ensure that the needs of individuals with CP continued to receive attention throughout their lives.
